accepted.simpleMeaning: a flight move in which an aircraft tilts sideways around its front-to-back axis, especially while turning
accepted.scope: This is not a row of objects or a place that keeps money; it is the sideways tilt of a plane in flight.
examples: The pilot made a steep bank to the left to avoid the storm.
During the turn the plane's bank reached forty degrees.
branchCoverage: a flight maneuver -> a flight move

examples: A bank of monitors filled the control room wall.

accepted.simpleMeaning: the supply of money that a casino or dealer holds to cover bets in some gambling games
accepted.scope: This is not a row of machines or the raised edge of a road; it is the money set aside to pay winning gamblers.
examples: The dealer drew on the bank to pay the winner.
He broke the bank at roulette with a single lucky bet.

accepted.simpleMeaning: a slope across a curved road or track, with the outer edge raised to reduce the outward pull of turning
accepted.scope: This is not the side of a river or a row of similar objects; it is the raised outer edge of a curve built for speed.
examples: The bank on the bend helps cars hold the road at speed.
Cyclists use the steep bank of the velodrome to carry speed through the turn.
branchCoverage: a slope in the turn of a road or track -> a slope across a curved road or track
